messages:
Maria Torres: heads-up — rewriting our internal incident comms templates + wording library. want the new set to be consistent for paging -> live mitigation -> handoff -> postmortem comms. starting a thread to capture fragments and land final copy.

Kevin Patel: great. do we want 2 tones: 'ops' (direct) and 'customer-friendly' (polished)? or a single neutral voice?

Maria Torres: leaning toward two variants. ops for on-call/internals, short and action-driven. customer-friendly for status page & customer-notify emails — fewer acronyms, clear impact/times.

Samir Kaur: +1. ops should include explicit action items, owner, ETA, and current mitigation steps. customer copy should focus on impact, affected scope, and next update time.

Jun Park: adding gov/regulated customers: we need a KMS/data mention checkbox in the template. even if not in the email, internal comms must call out data exposure risk explicitly if any.

Lisa Nguyen: can we standardize placeholders? suggestion: {{INCIDENT_ID}}, {{SEVERITY}}, {{STARTED_AT}}, {{AFFECTED_SERVICES}}, {{CUSTOMER_IMPACT}}, {{MITIGATION}}, {{NEXT_UPDATE_AT}}, {{POSTMORTEM_LINK}}

Maria Torres: yes — and keep them all-caps with double braces so they stand out in drafts. Also add {{OWNER}} and {{ONCALL_HANDOFF}} for the oncall snippets.

Kevin Patel: sketching ops template below. feedback welcome.

Kevin Patel: ```
[OPERATIONAL INCIDENT - {{INCIDENT_ID}}]
Severity: {{SEVERITY}}
Owner: {{OWNER}} (on-call: {{ONCALL}})
Started: {{STARTED_AT}}
Services: {{AFFECTED_SERVICES}}
Impact: {{CUSTOMER_IMPACT}}
Current status: {{MITIGATION}}
Actions required:
 - {{ACTION_1}} -> owner {{ACTION_1_OWNER}} (ETA: {{ACTION_1_ETA}})
 - {{ACTION_2}} -> owner {{ACTION_2_OWNER}}
Handoff status: {{ONCALL_HANDOFF}}
Next update: {{NEXT_UPDATE_AT}}
Runbook: {{RUNBOOK_LINK}}
```

Samir Kaur: that looks good. for severity mapping include short definitions in the header (S1 = total outage, S2 = partial but high impact, S3 = degraded). otherwise people argue about labels.

Maria Torres: adding severity definitions into 'ops' top. Also propose a one-line summary field for slack notifications so we can copy/paste into #incidents fast. e.g. `INCIDENT: {{INCIDENT_ID}} - {{ONE_LINE_SUMMARY}}`

Lisa Nguyen: customer-facing status page template draft:

Lisa Nguyen: ```
We are currently investigating an issue affecting {{AFFECTED_SERVICES}}. Some customers may experience {{CUSTOMER_IMPACT}}.

What we're doing: {{MITIGATION}}.
When we’ll share an update: {{NEXT_UPDATE_AT}} (or sooner).
Who to contact: support@redwood.ai (include your incident id: {{INCIDENT_ID}})
```

Jun Park: suggest adding clear 'Who is impacted' line (e.g. "Customers using Dedicated capacity in us-west-2") so customers can self-assess.

Maria Torres: agree. also recommend a short 'how this affects billing/SLAs' bullet to pre-empt questions. e.g., 'We are investigating potential latency impacts that may affect throughput; refunds or credits will be assessed after postmortem.' Keep it non-committal but proactive.

Kevin Patel: on on-call handoff phrasing — we need a tiny script that the outgoing on-call should paste. Proposed:

Kevin Patel: ```
Handoff: I, {{OUTGOING_ONCALL}}, handed off to {{INCOMING_ONCALL}} at {{HANDOFF_AT}}. Current status: {{CURRENT_STATUS}}. Open actions: {{OPEN_ACTIONS_SHORT}}.
```

Samir Kaur: +1. also add 'hot keys' for the on-call to quickly share: `!status` -> posts current status; `!page` -> notifies SRE pager. we should document these commands in the template for quick reference.

IncidentBot: automated note — next update reminder scheduled in 30m from now (use /incident remind to change). :bell:

Lisa Nguyen: language tone guidance for comms library:
 - Ops: terse, imperative, no filler. Assume readers are familiar with infra terms.
 - Customer: empathetic, plain language, no blame, set expectations for updates.
 - Postmortem/public: factual, timeline-first, root cause without jargon, mitigation & next steps.

Maria Torres: can we consolidate a checklist for 'customer notification' flow? rough list:
 - Confirm status & scope with on-call/owner
 - Draft status page blurb (customer template)
 - Internal 'ops' post in #incidents and escalate to eng-leads if S1
 - Notify CSMs + Account owners for affected customers (template email)
 - Decide public vs private notification (some customers may prefer direct emails)
 - Schedule next update times and who will send them

Jun Park: add security/compliance reviewer step for incidents involving data or auth. also add legal for regulated customers.

Kevin Patel: sample customer email template (short):

Kevin Patel: ```
Subject: [Redwood] Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — {Brief impact summary}

Hi {{CUSTOMER_CONTACT_NAME}},

We are investigating an issue affecting {{AFFECTED_SERVICES}} which may impact {{CUSTOMER_IMPACT}}. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation. We’ll send another update by {{NEXT_UPDATE_AT}}.

Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}
Support link: {{SUPPORT_PORTAL_LINK}}
Best,
Redwood Support
```

Lisa Nguyen: include a line for 'if this incident affects SLA or billing we will include details in the postmortem and contact your account team' — stops immediate billing questions during mitigation.

Maria Torres: formatting & tooling: final templates should live in /ops/incidents/templates.md and be accessible from the incident runbook. We should also add snippets as Slack message shortcuts for quicker posting (ops + customer variants).

Samir Kaur: can someone own the actual content rewrite? I can take the ops templates. Maria, can you own customer-facing templates and liaise with comms?

Maria Torres: yup I’ll own customer-facing and coordinate with Lisa (comms) for tone. Samir you own ops templates. Kevin can do the on-call snippets and automations (slash commands). Jun you own compliance checklist additions.

Kevin Patel: will add slash command examples and wire up a quick `/incident template ops` lookup in the bot.

Jun Park: I’ll draft the compliance checklist and add required approvals for data incidents.

Lisa Nguyen: I’ll create a short doc on tone + examples and sit with product comms to align.

Maria Torres: timeline — aim for initial PR with new templates by EOD Thursday, review Friday, deploy to snippets early next week. If anyone needs more time flag it here.

Samir Kaur: EOD Thursday works for me.

Kevin Patel: might need til Friday for slash command work — ok if template content merged first and commands follow.

Jun Park: Friday fine.

IncidentBot: reminder: please add `#incidents` thread link to the PR description for review automation.

Maria Torres: perfect. final note: please avoid hyperbolic language in customer copy (no 'we are devastated' etc). keep it clear, accountable, and short. I'll post a PR url here once ready. thanks all. :raised_hands:
